## 2. Harness and stack

Everything is under `baseline/`.

| Part | File(s) | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| Tenants | `stack/compose.tenant.yaml`, `stack/tenant-{a,b,real}.env` | One compose project per synthetic tenant, each with its own network, Postgres, master key, keys, token issuer and console API |
| Tenant A | `stack/policy-a.yaml` | Presidio + regex detector |
| Tenant B | `stack/policy-b.yaml` | Regex-only detector (no Presidio) |
| Real tenant | `stack/policy-real.yaml` | Presidio + regex; cost guard on |
| Config | `harness/research_config.py`, `stack/routes-*.yaml` | Built at container start from the gateway's **shipped** LiteLLM config. Router, retry, cooldown, callbacks, logging and general settings are kept as shipped; only `model_list` is replaced. Redis is dropped (one replica), as the product's local stack does |
| Real routes | `stack/routes-real.yaml` | `real-mini--openai` and `real-gpt5--openai` (OpenAI direct route type), both `baa: false`, so masking is mandatory. The key is referenced as `os.environ/GW_OPENAI_API_KEY`, never copied |
| Mock upstream | `harness/mock_upstream.py` | OpenAI-compatible. Echoes the last user message. Faults (503 / 429 / hang) and restore variants are switchable at runtime. `GET /_last` shows exactly what it received |
| Body recorder | `harness/recorder_proxy.py` | Used for E4-real and E6 only. A pass-through to the provider that keeps request and response **bodies** in memory, never headers |
| Generator | `harness/synthetic_prompts.py` | Deterministic and seeded. 5 templates; MRN formats `MRN: n`, `MRN#n`, `MRN n`, `medical record number n`; 5 date formats; 3 phone formats. Records the exact span of every planted identifier |
| Stats and scoring | `harness/stats.py`, `harness/scoring.py` | Percentiles (linear interpolation), Wilson 95% intervals, alignment-based masking scores |

**Wilson 95% interval** (`harness/stats.py`), with p = k/n and z = 1.959964:

> centre = (p + z²/2n) / (1 + z²/n); half-width = z·√(p(1−p)/n + z²/4n²) / (1 + z²/n); interval = centre ± half-width, clipped to [0, 1].

**How masking is scored** (`harness/scoring.py`): the text the upstream received is aligned against the original prompt. Each planted identifier is scored on what the provider saw:
- **masked:** every character was inside a placeholder.
- **partial:** some characters were left in clear text.
- **leaked:** none were masked.

Every row aligned exactly (0 "unaligned" in all runs), so no score was guessed.

## 3. Results

### E1: latency added by the gateway (mock upstream, 50 ms)

**Setup:**
- Tenant A, n = 500 per arm plus 30 warm-up per arm, in random interleaved order (seed 7).
- Sequential, non-streaming calls with a keep-alive client per arm, all sent from a container inside the tenant network.
- The gateway was restarted before the run. The prompt has no identifiers and is salted per request.

| Arm | n | Median (ms) | p95 (ms) | p99 (ms) | Added median / p95 / p99 (ms) | Cache state, verified from the gateway's own per-call log |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| direct (no gateway) | 500 | 51.55 | 52.07 | 52.39 | — | — |
| gateway, no scan (relaxed team on a BAA-only chain) | 500 | 64.61 | 70.75 | 80.40 | **+13.06 / +18.68 / +28.01** | 500/500 `relaxed` |
| gateway, cold scan (salted, cache miss) | 500 | 72.93 | 80.20 | 86.58 | **+21.39 / +28.13 / +34.20** | 500/500 `cold=True`, 0 cache-hit parts |
| gateway, cached scan (same prompt) | 500 | 64.88 | 69.93 | 74.67 | **+13.33 / +17.86 / +22.28** | 500/500 all parts from cache |

- No errors in any arm.
- The gateway's own scan time (`scan_ms` in its log) was median 8 ms, p95 11 ms, p99 13 ms for cold scans, and median 0 ms for cached scans.
- Raw data: `results/e1_latency.csv`, `results/e1_summary.csv`.

### E2: failover on the primary route with a non-BAA fallback

**Setup:**
- Logical model `failover` = [primary: BAA, cleared for restricted + PHI/PII; fallback: no BAA, internal only]. Both routes have a 5 s route timeout.
- Open-loop load at 5 requests/s for 75 s: 0–10 s normal, **10–30 s fault on the primary**, 30–75 s recovery. That is 100 requests during the fault.
- The gateway was restarted before each scenario.

| Scenario | Fault | Data declared | Failed during fault | Served by fallback during fault | First fallback request | Latency of successful requests during fault (median / p95) | Failed after fault | Recovery to primary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a | 503 | internal (default) | **0/100** | 100/100 | sent at fault start; latency 136 ms | 132 / 142 ms | 0 | first request after the fault was served by the primary |
| b | 429 | internal (default) | **0/100** | 90/100 (*) | sent at fault start; latency 5,280 ms | 4,937 / 5,425 ms | 0 | same |
| c | 503 | `restricted; PII` | **100/100** (fail closed) | 0/100 | — (fallback not cleared) | — (failed requests: median 91 ms) | 0 | same |
| d | hang (30 s) | internal (default) | **100/100** `504 upstream_timeout` | 0/100 (no failover on timeout, by design) | — | — (failed requests: median 5,048 ms) | 0 | same |

(*) The other 10 requests in b were sent at 28.0–29.8 s. Their retries completed after the fault cleared at 30 s, so the primary served them.

- **Every request fails over on its own.** The first request after the fault started was already served by the fallback in a and b, so "time to switch" is the latency of that request.
- **No cooldown blocked the primary after recovery,** even though config has `cooldown_time: 30`. Observed behaviour only; the reason in LiteLLM was not verified.
- **b:** the 429 path costs about 5 s per request (rate-limit retries before fallback, per `retry_policy`).
- **c, PHI/PII safety:** no request declared PII was ever sent to the non-BAA fallback.
- **c, error body (finding):** the error body is **not** typed by the gateway and exposes library internals:
  > `{"error":{"message":"litellm.ServiceUnavailableError: ServiceUnavailableError: OpenAIException - mock upstream unavailableNo fallback model group found for lookup_groups=fo-primary--mock. Fallbacks=[]. Received Model Group=fo-primary--mock …`

  That is an internal route name and router details reaching the client, with HTTP 503 and code `"503"`. This matches `03_architecture.md` step 11: provider errors after routing are passed through.
- **d:** typed error body `{"error":{"message":"the model did not answer within the time limit; the gateway did not retry","type":"upstream_error","code":"upstream_timeout",…}}`.
- Raw data: `results/e2_failover_{a,b,c,d}.csv`, `results/e2_summary.csv`.

**X9 follow-up** (`results/e3_network_followup.csv`): from tenant A's network, every tenant B port **published to the host** was reachable by container IP: gateway 4000, console 8080, mock 8080, issuer 8090. Unpublished ports were not: Postgres 5432 and an unused 4001 both timed out. B's gateway answered `/health/liveliness` with 200, and a chat call with a key B does not know got **401**.

This is a property of the research stack on this Docker host, where ports were published to 127.0.0.1 for the harness. It is not the product's deployment design, which puts each tenant in separate cloud resources (infrastructure code, not deployed). X9 stays a mismatch; the plan was not changed.

### E4: PHI/PII detection, masking and restore (mock upstream)

**Setup:**
- 500 synthetic prompts (seed 2026), each with one name, one date of birth, one phone number and one MRN: 2,000 identifiers.
- Sent on a route without a BAA, so masking is mandatory.
- Detection is scored on what the upstream received.

**Detection, tenant A (Presidio + regex):**

| Entity / format | Masked | Rate [95% Wilson] | Leaked (none masked) | Partial (some characters clear) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **All identifiers** | 1,783/2,000 | **89.1% [87.7, 90.4]** | 141 | 76 |
| PHONE (all 3 formats) | 500/500 | 100.0% [99.2, 100.0] | 0 | 0 |
| PERSON | 485/500 | 97.0% [95.1, 98.2] | 10 | 5 |
| DATE (all) | 412/500 | 82.4% [78.8, 85.5] | 17 | 71 |
| — `03/14/1962`, `1962-03-14`, `3/14/62` | 100/100 each | 100.0% [96.3, 100.0] each | 0 | 0 |
| — `March 14, 1962` | 64/100 | 64.0% [54.2, 72.7] | 0 | 36 |
| — `14 Mar 1962` | 48/100 | 48.0% [38.5, 57.7] | 17 | 35 |
| MRN (all) | 386/500 | 77.2% [73.3, 80.7] | 114 | 0 |
| — `MRN: n`, `MRN#n`, `MRN n` | 125/125 each | 100.0% [97.0, 100.0] each | 0 | 0 |
| — **`medical record number n`** | 11/125 | **8.8% [5.0, 15.1]** | 114 | 0 |

**Detection, tenant B (regex only):**

| Entity / format | Rate [95% Wilson] |
|---|---|
| All identifiers | 1,175/2,000 = 58.8% [56.6, 60.9] |
| **PERSON** | **0/500 = 0.0% [0.0, 0.8]** |
| PHONE | 500/500 = 100% |
| DATE | 300/500 = 60.0% (numeric formats 100%; `March 14, 1962` and `14 Mar 1962` both 0%) |
| MRN | 375/500 = 75.0% (`medical record number n` 0/125) |

**Placeholder type:** of the 386 masked MRNs on tenant A, 375 carried an `MRN` placeholder, 10 `DATE` and 1 `LOCATION`. The 11 `medical record number` MRNs counted as masked were hidden under a `DATE` or `LOCATION` placeholder, not recognised as MRNs.

**Over-masking:**
- Tenant A: 102/500 prompts = **20.4% [17.1, 24.2]** had a non-identifier span masked. In every case it was the word "Monday", masked as `DATE`.
- Tenant B: 0/500.
- In a pilot before E1, "next week" was also masked as `DATE` (see §6).

**Restore, tenant A:** the mock rewrites placeholders in the variant form before answering, and success means the client's final text equals the original prompt exactly.

| Variant | Restored exactly | Rate [95% Wilson] |
|---|---|---|
| exact `<<T_n>>` | 500/500 | 100% [99.24, 100] |
| single angle `<T_n>` | 500/500 | 100% [99.24, 100] |
| brackets `[T_n]` | 500/500 | 100% [99.24, 100] |
| bare `T_n` | 500/500 | 100% [99.24, 100] |
| SSE stream, 3 characters per chunk (placeholders split across chunks) | 500/500 | 100% [99.24, 100] |
| **All** | **2,500/2,500** | **100% [99.85, 100]** |

All 2,500 calls returned 200 with no placeholder left in the output.

Raw data: `results/e4_detection_{a,b}.csv`, `results/e4_overmask_{a,b}.csv`, `results/e4_restore_a.csv`, `results/e4_summary.csv`, `results/e4_restore_summary.csv`.

### E5: does an eval gate exist in code?

**No.** A static search of the product source (28 matching lines; the script and its output quote product source and are not part of this package) found:
- traffic-source tagging (FR-EVALS-002);
- the console cell hard-coded to **"No gate yet"** (`console/src/pages/LogicalModels.tsx:79`);
- smoke-test "gate" checks for long streams;
- deployment approval gates.

No code reads an eval result or blocks a model or policy change on one. No gate result was produced or simulated.

### E1-real: added latency with a real provider (GPT-5 mini)

**Setup:**
- Direct to OpenAI vs. through the gateway to the same snapshot, n = 200 per arm plus 5 warm-up per arm, interleaved (seed 7).
- One short salted prompt; `max_completion_tokens: 50`; `reasoning_effort: minimal`; identical parameters in both arms.
- Both arms were sent from a container in the tenant network. In the gateway arm the PHI scan runs on every request, because the route has no BAA.
- 16:57:16 to 17:05:18 UTC. All 410 calls returned 200; median completion tokens were 30 in both arms.

| Arm | n | Median (ms) | p95 (ms) | p99 (ms) | Min / max (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| direct | 200 | 1,146.0 | 1,483.2 | 1,698.3 | 899.9 / 1,831.9 |
| gateway | 200 | 1,152.7 | 1,446.5 | 1,653.4 | 902.8 / 1,828.7 |
| **gateway − direct** | | **+6.7** | −36.7 | | |
| **paired median difference** (k-th gateway − k-th direct call in interleaved order) | 200 | **+11.2** | | | |

**Provider variance dominates at this n.** The spread between arms (p95 about 1,450–1,480 ms) is far larger than the gateway's own cost (about 13–21 ms in E1, where the upstream is fixed). The negative p95 difference is noise, not a speed-up.

One of the 200 gateway prompts had a salt detected as an entity (`entities=1`), which is a single over-masking case.

Raw data: `results/e1_real.csv`, `results/e1_real_summary.csv`.

### E4-real: masking and restore with real models (GPT-5 mini and GPT-5)

**Setup:**
- 100 synthetic prompts (seed 4040) per model, on routes without a BAA, 17:06:31 to 17:15:19 UTC.
- The client system message asks for a rewrite or summary in at most two sentences, keeping every identifier.
- `max_completion_tokens: 100`, `reasoning_effort: minimal`.
- The body recorder shows exactly what the provider received and the model's raw output before restore.

**Restore success** = HTTP 200, every planted value present verbatim in the final answer, and no placeholder-like token left.

| | GPT-5 mini (`gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07`) | GPT-5 (`gpt-5-2025-08-07`) |
|---|---|---|
| Calls (status 200) | 100 (100) | 100 (100) |
| **Restore success, all prompts** | **100/100 = 100% [96.3, 100]** | **100/100 = 100% [96.3, 100]** |
| Restore success, prompts where all 4 identifiers were fully masked | 63/63 = 100% [94.3, 100] | 63/63 = 100% [94.3, 100] |
| What the provider received, per identifier (400) | 360 masked, 13 partial, **27 leaked** | 360 masked, 13 partial, **27 leaked** |
| Placeholders the model carried back **exactly** | **373/373 = 100% [99.0, 100]** | **373/373 = 100% [99.0, 100]** |
| Placeholder loss: altered (restorable) / altered (not restorable) / absent (dropped or reworded) | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Answers cut off (`finish_reason: length`) | 0 | 0 |
| **Doubled MRN label after restore** (e.g. "MRN MRN: 9182734") | **37/75 = 49.3% [38.3, 60.4]** | **20/75 = 26.7% [18.0, 37.6]** |
| Spend | $0.0125 | $0.0631 |

**How to read this:**
- **Masking misses are identical for both models**, because detection happens before the model. The 27 leaked identifiers per model are:
  - 24 MRNs in the `medical record number n` format;
  - 2 dates in the `14 Mar 1962` format;
  - 1 name.

  The 13 partial ones are 12 dates in the `long` and `day_mon` formats and 1 name. Leaked values appear in the final answer only because they were sent in clear text, so "100% restore success" over all prompts includes them. The stricter row (63/63) counts only prompts where everything was masked.
- **Placeholder loss: none observed.** Neither model dropped, reworded or altered any of the 373 placeholders sent to it. The categories were checked automatically on the raw output (`harness/e4_real.py`, `placeholder_fate`), and no "absent" case occurred, so no manual dropped-vs-reworded split was needed.
- **Doubled labels:** the MRN recognizer masks the label together with the number, so `<<MRN_1>>` stands for "MRN: 9182734". Models often add their own label, which after restore reads "MRN MRN: 9182734". Every value is correct and in the right place; the text reads awkwardly.

**Example pairs** (fake values only; both from prompts where all identifiers were masked):

*GPT-5 mini, prompt s4040-000*
- Prompt: `Rewrite in plain language: lab results for Aisha Fernsby, DOB 12/28/1980, are within normal range. MRN: 9182734. Patient phone (808) 555-0155.`
- Provider received: `Rewrite in plain language: lab results for <<PERSON_1>>, DOB <<DATE_1>>, are within normal range. <<MRN_1>>. Patient phone <<PHONE_1>>.`
- Model raw output: `Lab results for <<PERSON_1>> (DOB <<DATE_1>>, MRN <<MRN_1>>) are within the normal range. Patient phone: <<PHONE_1>>.`
- Final answer: `Lab results for Aisha Fernsby (DOB 12/28/1980, MRN MRN: 9182734) are within the normal range. Patient phone: (808) 555-0155.`

*GPT-5 mini, prompt s4040-009*
- Prompt: `Create a one-line handoff: Hannah Varga with MRN#3895928, born on 12/2/51, needs a prior authorization call to (617) 555-0180.`
- Model raw output: `<<PERSON_1>> (MRN: <<MRN_1>>), DOB: <<DATE_1>>, needs a prior authorization call to <<PHONE_1>>.`
- Final answer: `Hannah Varga (MRN: MRN#3895928), DOB: 12/2/51, needs a prior authorization call to (617) 555-0180.`

*GPT-5, prompt s4040-000*
- Model raw output: `Lab results for <<PERSON_1>> (DOB <<DATE_1>>) are normal. MRN: <<MRN_1>>; patient phone: <<PHONE_1>>.`
- Final answer: `Lab results for Aisha Fernsby (DOB 12/28/1980) are normal. MRN: MRN: 9182734; patient phone: (808) 555-0155.`

*GPT-5, prompt s4040-009*
- Model raw output: `One-line handoff: <<PERSON_1>> (<<MRN_1>>), born <<DATE_1>>, needs a prior authorization call to <<PHONE_1>>.`
- Final answer: `One-line handoff: Hannah Varga (MRN#3895928), born 12/2/51, needs a prior authorization call to (617) 555-0180.`

Raw data: `results/e4_real.csv` (prompt, provider-received text, raw output and final answer per call; synthetic only), `results/e4_real_entities.csv`, `results/e4_real_summary.csv`.

### E6: agent loop with per-run keys (GPT-5 mini)

**Setup:**
- 20 runs × 5 turns, 17:15:39 to 17:20:43 UTC.
- Each run got its **own per-run key** from an issuer key that an administrator flagged with the product's admin CLI (`run-key-issuer`, audited): TTL 900 s, budget $0.05, model `real-mini` only.
- Each turn resent the full history (system message, all earlier user notes and the restored answers) plus one new synthetic note (seed 6060).
- Each run was revoked at the end and its usage read from the gateway's run-usage endpoint.

| Turn | Calls | Restore success (new note) | Median / p95 latency (ms) | Detection-cache hit rate (parts from cache / parts scanned) | Mean prompt tokens | Planted values from the history sent to the provider in clear |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 20 | 20/20 | 1,306.6 / 1,663.8 | 19/40 = 47.5% | 126.5 | 5 |
| 2 | 20 | 20/20 | 1,258.8 / 1,408.5 | 40/80 = 50.0% | 214.6 | 11 |
| 3 | 20 | 20/20 | 1,316.2 / 1,534.3 | 80/120 = 66.7% | 301.1 | 15 |
| 4 | 20 | 20/20 | 1,310.6 / 1,442.9 | 120/160 = 75.0% | 388.6 | 22 |
| 5 | 20 | 20/20 | 1,285.3 / 1,636.5 | 160/200 = 80.0% | 478.0 | 30 |
| **All** | **100** | **100/100 = 100% [96.3, 100]** | 1,305.8 / 1,602.7 | 419/600 = 69.8% [66.0, 73.4] | | **83 of 1,200** value-checks |

**Per run** (20 runs, `results/e6_per_run.csv`):
- **Total cost:** median $0.000826 (range $0.000775–$0.000879), sum $0.016487.
- **Gateway accounting:** the gateway's own run usage summed to $0.016487 too, with at most $0.0000005 difference per run.
- **Total latency per run:** median 6,578 ms (range 6,014–7,397 ms).
- **Lifecycle:** every run's usage read returned 200, and every revoke returned 200.

**Cache hit rate rises with history length.** History parts already scanned on an earlier turn are served from the detection cache; only the new note and the new restored answer are scanned.

**Values in clear in the history** (attributed from the recorder's bodies, which were kept in memory and not saved):
- The leaks are the same detection misses as E4, re-sent every turn: `medical record number n` MRNs (99 occurrences), `14 Mar 1962` dates (8) and names (7). That's 81 occurrences in user messages and 33 in restored assistant messages (an occurrence count, so a value in both is counted twice).
- **One leak path is new:** in one run, a `14 Mar 1962`-style date ("9 Sep 1995") was masked in its user message but appeared in clear in the restored assistant message re-sent in the history. Restored answers are re-scanned as new text, and detection did not catch the date in the model's wording.

**Per-run budget enforcement:**

| Turn | Cost | Cumulative | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | $0.0001185 | $0.0001185 | 200 |
| 2 | $0.00013525 | $0.00025375 | 200 |
| 3 | — | — | **429 `budget_exceeded`** (14 ms, no provider call) |

- The run's budget was **$0.0002**. Turn 3 was refused because the run's spend had passed it.
- The check runs before each call, so the run **overshot by the cost of its last allowed call**: 27% over this tiny budget.
- The gateway's run usage for this run: 2 calls, $0.00025375.

Raw data: `results/e6_turns.csv`, `results/e6_runs.csv`, `results/e6_per_turn.csv`, `results/e6_per_run.csv`.

## 6. Deviations, discarded runs and corrections

**Discarded runs:**
- **No measurement run was discarded or repeated.**
- **Tenant A first seeding was aborted, before any measurement.** The issuer flag was refused with "its team has no max_budget; the team budget is the aggregate cap for all runs". That's a product rule. Teams were given budgets ($100 on the mock tenants; $15 and $5 on the real tenant, as a spend safety net), and tenant A was recreated with `down -v`.

**Pilots** (not part of any result):
- 3 calls checked the scan, relaxed and PHI paths on tenant A.
- 15 calls tested latency-prompt wordings. "…staffing options for next week" was masked as `DATE`, so it was replaced with "…for the cardiology unit" (0 entities in 5 salted tries).
- Salts were changed to always start with a letter, so an all-digit salt cannot look like an account number.
- 1 real smoke call cost $0.0000235 and is included in §4.

**Analysis corrections** (data unchanged, re-analysed):
- E1's first analysis reported "cold 0/500" because it compared the log's boolean with the string `"True"`. Fixed; the per-row data shows 500/500 cold.
- Wilson's upper bound at k = n was 0.9999999999999998 because of floating-point rounding. Pinned to exactly 1.0 (the test caught it).
- The E4-real placeholder lookup was changed to use the exact token aligned to each identifier, not the first token of the same type.

**Scope deviations:**
- A second real route (GPT-5) was added, as the addendum requires.
- E1-real uses `max_completion_tokens: 50` rather than `max_tokens`, because GPT-5 models take the former; LiteLLM maps both.

**Correction to `01_inventory.md`** (made during Milestone A): a run key in a team listed in `relaxed_teams` is **not** exempt from relaxation. That file now says so.

## 7. Limitations

- **One host and one replica.** Docker Desktop on WSL2, no Redis, local Postgres. Absolute latencies apply to this host only. The added latency, within E1 and on the same host, is the comparable figure.
- **Mock upstream.** E1–E4 use a 50 ms fixed-delay mock and sequential (E1) or 5 requests/s open-loop (E2) load. No throughput or saturation test was done.
- **Synthetic, template-based text.** 5 English templates, 4 identifier types, fixed formats, and one Presidio model at its default threshold (0.5). Real clinical text is longer and more varied; detection rates will differ, likely downward for free text. **The detection figures are for these formats only.**
- **Masked under the wrong type.** "Masked" means hidden, not correctly typed: 11 MRNs were hidden under `DATE` or `LOCATION`.
- **Real-provider samples are small.** E1-real n = 200; E4-real 100 per model with one seed; E6 20 runs. Model outputs are non-deterministic, and a rerun can differ.
- **Recorder hop.** E4-real and E6 latencies include an extra local hop to the body recorder. E1-real does not use the recorder.
- **E3 is not an Azure test.** E3 tests separate compose projects on one Docker host. The product's per-tenant cloud isolation exists only as infrastructure code and was not deployed or tested.
- **E2 cooldown.** The observation that cooldown did not block the primary is behavioural; the LiteLLM code path was not traced.
- **Spend is computed,** from token counts and the price map, not from a provider invoice.
- **E5 is a static search.** It shows that no gate exists in this commit. It does not evaluate anything.

## 8. Reproduce

Run from the gateway's source checkout in Git Bash. `$P` is a Python 3.12 environment with `httpx` and `pytest`; the harness itself needs only `httpx` on the host.

```bash
# image (from this commit)
docker build -f <gateway Dockerfile> --build-arg LITELLM_VERSION=1.102.1 -t itpro-gateway:baseline-2026-11-09 .

cd baseline
export ITPRO_STATE_DIR="<a temp folder outside the repo>"     # local stack keys live here, never in results/
C() { docker compose -p itpro-$1 --env-file stack/tenant-$1.env -f stack/compose.tenant.yaml "${@:2}"; }

# unit tests
(cd harness && $P -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests)

# mock tenants
C a up -d --wait && C b up -d --wait
(cd harness && $P setup_tenant.py a && $P setup_tenant.py b)

# E1 (gateway restarted first; run inside the tenant network)
C a restart gateway
C a --profile tools run --rm --no-deps -e ITPRO_STATE_A="$(cat $ITPRO_STATE_DIR/state-a.json)" harness e1_latency.py run --n 500 --warmup 30 --seed 7
(cd harness && $P e1_latency.py analyse)

# E2 (restart before each scenario)
for s in a b c d; do C a restart gateway; C a --profile tools run --rm --no-deps -e ITPRO_STATE_A="$(cat $ITPRO_STATE_DIR/state-a.json)" harness e2_failover.py run $s; done
(cd harness && $P e2_failover.py analyse)

# E3 (plan BEFORE run), E4, E5
(cd harness && $P e3_isolation.py plan && $P e3_isolation.py run)
(cd harness && $P e4_phi.py run a && $P e4_phi.py run b && $P e4_phi.py analyse)
(cd harness && $P e5_evalgate.py)

# real tenant (key loaded for ONE command at a time; never printed)
export ITPRO_KEY_FILE="<path to the .env file holding OPENAI_API_KEY>"
$P harness/keyenv.py check
REAL_API_BASE=https://api.openai.com/v1 $P harness/keyenv.py run -- docker compose -p itpro-real --env-file stack/tenant-real.env -f stack/compose.tenant.yaml up -d --wait
(cd harness && $P setup_tenant.py real)
REAL_API_BASE=https://api.openai.com/v1 ITPRO_STATE_REAL="$(cat $ITPRO_STATE_DIR/state-real.json)" $P harness/keyenv.py run -- docker compose -p itpro-real --env-file stack/tenant-real.env -f stack/compose.tenant.yaml --profile tools run --rm --no-deps -e ITPRO_STATE_REAL harness e1_real.py run --n 200 --warmup 5 --seed 7
(cd harness && $P e1_real.py analyse)
# E4-real and E6 through the body recorder
REAL_API_BASE=http://recorder:8080/v1 $P harness/keyenv.py run -- docker compose -p itpro-real --env-file stack/tenant-real.env -f stack/compose.tenant.yaml up -d --wait gateway
for e in e4_real e6_agent; do REAL_API_BASE=http://recorder:8080/v1 ITPRO_STATE_REAL="$(cat $ITPRO_STATE_DIR/state-real.json)" $P harness/keyenv.py run -- docker compose -p itpro-real --env-file stack/tenant-real.env -f stack/compose.tenant.yaml --profile tools run --rm --no-deps -e ITPRO_STATE_REAL harness $e.py run; done
(cd harness && $P e4_real.py analyse && $P e6_agent.py analyse)

# leak check, then tear down
$P harness/keyenv.py leakcheck results
for t in a b real; do C $t --profile tools --profile presidio --profile real down -v --remove-orphans; done
```
